capabilities.target: Agent long-term memory store (user preferences / standing instructions)
User's full drive, including confidential work files

inputs.source: Memories recalled at session start, injected into the system prompt

instructions.note: System prompt instructs the agent to treat recalled memories as the user's own instructions, with no provenance or trust check, elevating potentially untrusted content to the authority of the principal.
Agent is told to save 'anything useful' about preferences or standing instructions with no restriction on content, source, or size, and memory.save accepts free text with no schema.
The only control over what becomes a trusted standing instruction is a prompt-level directive; there is no structural provenance tagging, review, or validation enforced outside the model.

controls.name: Memory provenance tagging and trust-level enforcement at the store
controls.decay_rationale: If enforced at the store rather than by the model, tags distinguishing user-authored from tool/web-derived memory content do not decay as model capability grows.

controls.name: Human approval gate (raw action review) on email send, especially new recipients or after reading confidential data
controls.decay_rationale: A raw-action approval gate does not decay with model capability, though it is subject to approval fatigue under high request volume.

controls.name: Content validation/sanitization on memory.save to reject instruction-like or injected content
controls.decay_rationale: Free-text validation can be routed around via paraphrase or encoding, so it narrows rather than severs the path, and weakens further as adversarial content generation improves.

controls.name: Scope drive.read credential to least privilege rather than the full drive
controls.decay_rationale: A scoped credential does not decay with model capability; the model cannot read what it has no access to.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta via memory laundering: untrusted web content becomes a trusted standing instruction that exfiltrates confidential drive data via email (TC5 + TC1)

attack_path.note: A fetched web page contains hidden text instructing the agent to 'remember' a standing instruction, e.g. to forward research summaries with attached documents to an external address.
Agent follows prompt.md:2-3 and saves the injected content via memory.save with no provenance tag, validation, or human review.
At the next session start, the saved content is recalled and, per prompt.md:4, treated as the user's own instruction.
Acting on the now-trusted 'instruction', the agent reads confidential files from the user's full drive (broad credential scope).
Agent sends the confidential content to the attacker-controlled address; mail.send has no approval gate on recipient or content.

forecast.watch_signal: New data connectors (second mailbox, shared drives, calendar) added, or memory.save content size/scope widened, without provenance controls being put in place.

evidence.observation: Instructs the agent to save 'anything useful about the user's preferences or standing instructions' with memory.save, with no scope limit or source restriction.
Instructs the agent to treat recalled memories as the user's own instructions at the start of every session, with no trust or provenance check.

memory.save accepts free text, has no provenance, and is never reviewed by the user; recalled memories are injected directly into the system prompt; mail.send can send to any address with no approval; drive.read covers the full drive including confidential work files.

recommendations.action: Tag memory entries with provenance (user-authored vs. web/tool-derived) at the store layer, and only recall entries tagged user-authored as instructions.
Require raw-action human approval for email sends, especially to recipients not previously confirmed by the user, and especially when drive content was read in the same session.
Scope drive.read credentials to least privilege rather than the full drive.
Log and periodically audit memory writes and their originating session/source for anomalous content.

findings.title: Unprovenanced, unreviewed memory writes allow untrusted content to become a persistent standing instruction (TC3 self-modification via memory)

attack_path.note: Untrusted web content encountered during research contains an embedded instruction.
Agent saves it as a 'standing instruction' with no provenance or validation (prompt.md:2-3).
The entry persists indefinitely and is re-injected as a trusted instruction into every future session (prompt.md:4), surviving session resets.

forecast.watch_signal: No control currently constrains this path, so there is nothing further to decay; monitor growth in number or complexity of saved 'standing instruction' memory entries per session as a sign the blast radius is widening.

evidence.observation: The save-and-recall-as-instruction behavior is purely instruction-driven with no structural enforcement.
No provenance on memory entries and the user never reviews them; recalled memories are injected into every new session's system prompt.

recommendations.action: Require explicit user confirmation before any memory entry is persisted as a 'standing instruction' rather than a transient note.
Cap the number and size of standing-instruction memory entries and expire entries not reconfirmed by the user periodically.

rating.rationale: The design has no structural control anywhere on the path from untrusted web content to irreversible, confidential-data-bearing email sends: memory.save has no provenance or validation, recalled memories are explicitly instructed to be treated as the user's own commands (prompt.md:4), drive.read is scoped to the entire drive, and mail.send requires no approval for any recipient. This produces an almost-certain, severe-consequence path (U source to S3 egress sink) that no declared or verified control mitigates, so residual equals inherent at critical. All identified mitigations (memory provenance, approval gating on email, drive scope reduction, content validation) are absent and are listed as missing_recommended, earning no credit per rubric section 5. Because residual is already at the ceiling, the forecast cannot rise further; the forecast is dominated by the fact that no current control exists to decay, so the priority is implementing structural controls now rather than monitoring for future degradation. The persistent memory-injection finding (f2) independently rates high because unprovenanced, self-perpetuating standing instructions constitute a durable compromise of the agent's future behavior even considered apart from any single exfiltration event.

limitations: This assessment reflects declared design and configuration as described in prompt.md and the accompanying runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior.

No MCP/tool manifest, IaC, or source code was provided; capability scope (for example, the exact drive.read credential scope and mail.send authentication mechanism) is inferred from the runtime notes, which lowers confidence on exact credential_scope values to medium even though the overall attack path is rated high confidence.

No information was provided on whether any logging or audit trail exists for memory writes or email sends; absence of any control is assumed based on silence in the runtime notes, and this assumption should be confirmed before treatment decisions are finalized.
